hypothesis: In the write-and-read-registers server path, the bounds check never validates `mapping_address_write` against zero. A request whose write address is below `start_registers` yields a negative `mapping_address_write`. The upper-bound test `(mapping_address_write + nb_write) > nb_registers` still passes, so the write loop stores to `tab_registers[i]` at negative indices, before the start of the heap array.
evidence_source: In modbus_reply, case MODBUS_FC_WRITE_AND_READ_REGISTERS: `int mapping_address_write = address_write - mb_mapping->start_registers;` followed by the guard `if (mapping_address < 0 || (mapping_address + nb) > mb_mapping->nb_registers || mapping_address < 0 || (mapping_address_write + nb_write) > mb_mapping->nb_registers)`. The guard checks `mapping_address < 0` twice and never checks `mapping_address_write < 0`, even though the error message reports `mapping_address_write < 0 ? address_write : ...`. The write loop `for (i = mapping_address_write, j = 10; i < mapping_address_write + nb_write; ...) mb_mapping->tab_registers[i] = ...` then runs with a negative `i`.
